subject: giant dam strait
title: What If We Dammed Gibraltar to Drain the Mediterranean? A 1920s Plan

scenes.text: What if we drained the Mediterranean on purpose? In the 1920s, a German architect drew up the plan.
Herman Sörgel's Atlantropa: a dam across the Strait of Gibraltar, foundations 300 meters high, a 400-meter tower on top.
Seal off the Atlantic and evaporation does the rest: the sea drops 100 meters in the west, 200 in the east.
That would uncover more new land than the whole of France, and the dam's turbines could generate 50,000 megawatts.
Venice would sit by a lake 500 kilometers from the sea. Genoa and Marseille would be stranded.
He campaigned for it until his death in 1952. Nobody built it, and the water is still there.

description:
What if we dammed the Strait of Gibraltar to drain the Mediterranean? In the late 1920s, German architect Herman Sörgel proposed exactly that: Atlantropa. A dam with 300-meter foundations would seal off the Atlantic, evaporation would lower the sea by 100 meters in the west and 200 in the east over about a century, exposing more new land than the area of France, while turbines at Gibraltar generated around 50,000 megawatts.
Venice would be left beside a lake 500 kilometers from the coast. Sörgel promoted the plan until his death in 1952; it was never built.
